title: 2024 AMC 10B Problem 15
statement: A list of \(9\) real numbers consists of \(1,\) \(2.2,\) \(3.2,\) \(5.2,\) \(6.2,\) \(7,\) as well as \(x,\) \(y,\) \(z\) with \(x \le y \le z.\) The range of the list is \(7,\) and the mean and median are both positive integers. How many ordered triples \((x, y, z)\) are possible?

solutions.text:
The six fixed numbers total \(24.8.\) If the mean is the integer \(k,\) then \(x+y+z=9k-24.8.\) Because the fixed entries already run from \(1\) to \(7,\) the range condition gives three cases.

If \(z\le7,\) then \(x=0.\) The bounds on \(y+z\) force \(k=3\) or \(4.\) For \(k=3,\) the median is \(2.2;\) for \(k=4,\) we have \(y+z=11.2,\) so \(y\ge4.2\) and the median is integral only when \(y=5,\) giving \((x,y,z)=(0,5,6.2).\)

If \(x\ge1,\) then \(z=8.\) Here \(k=4\) gives median \(3.2.\) For \(k=5,\) we have \(x+y=12.2;\) the median is integral only when \(x=6,\) giving \((6,6.2,8).\)

The remaining case has \(0<x<1\) and \(z=x+7.\) The total lies between \(31.8\) and \(41.8,\) so \(k=4\) and \(y=4.2-2x.\) The median can be an integer only when \(y=4,\) giving \((0.1,4,7.1).\) Hence exactly \(3\) ordered triples work. Thus, C is the correct answer.
hints: The six given numbers sum to \(24.8,\) so \(x + y + z\) must make the total a multiple of \(9\)
Range \(7\) fixes the smallest and largest values; then require the \(5\)th smallest number to be a positive integer
